Global Trade and Demand
Assesses global trade intensity and capital flows by combining USD regime signals, macro positioning (for example, supply stress), and speculative risk tone.

Regime Assessment:

  • Regime: Expansionary / Risk-Positive.
  • Regime Confidence Index: High Confidence.
  • The regime is fragile.

Why This Regime:

  • A rebound in speculative breadth drives the risk-on tone (1).
  • Persistent energy supply stress and metals momentum support cyclical expansion (2).
  • High-weight tactical and cyclical drivers are currently aligned.
  • The USD Index was downweighted due to extreme threshold proximity and high volatility (3).

Alignment & Tensions:

  • The risk-on tone aligns with upward-biased commodity price paths (1)(2).
  • A weakening dollar regime provides supportive global liquidity conditions (3).
  • Tensions exist due to rapid fluctuations between positioning thresholds (1).
  • These tensions do not overturn the call as aggregate speculative counts remain positive.

Scenario Balance:

  • Dominant scenario: Risk-on persistence supported by expanding net speculative positioning (1).
  • Primary upside risk: Transition to "Strong Risk-On" if positioning z-scores exceed 1.0 (1).
  • Primary downside risk: Shift to "Global Slowdown" if metals positioning rotates to net-short (2).

What Would Change the Regime:

  • The market tone z-score declining below 0.5 triggers a shift to neutral (1).
  • A USD monthly close above 120.46 invalidates the weakening dollar regime (3).

Global Risk-On / Risk-Off Positioning Tone

Signal Summary:

  • Given the net_tone of 0.0375 and a CoT_Market_Tone_z of 0.866, this setup aligns with Upward-biased price paths and Normal volatility, where the dominant risk is Trend continuation, not Regime shift, based on the positive speculative sentiment rule (1).
  • The signal is currently in a "Risk-On" regime, reflecting a recovery in speculative breadth following a one-week dip into neutral territory (1).
  • Conviction Band: Medium; Interpretation Confidence: High Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Volatile; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • A z-score between 0.5 and 1.0 signifies "Risk-On" conditions and positive speculative sentiment (1).
  • The "net_tone" metric, which calculates the ratio of crowded longs vs crowded shorts, determines the aggregate breadth (1).
  • Rising signal values indicate a transition toward risk-on/expansion regimes (1).
  • Global Risk-On / Risk-Off Positioning Tone (2026-05-12) (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the rebound in crowded_long_count (from 84 to 92) relative to stable short positioning (1).
  • Momentum shows stabilization after a sharp deceleration from the extreme "Strong Risk-On" peaks (>1.0 z-score) observed in March (1).
  • Internal offsets: None; long and short counts are moving in alignment with a risk-on recovery (1).
  • Conditional Invalidation: A decline in CoT_Market_Tone_z below 0.5 would trigger a shift to a Neutral regime (1).
  • The signal is currently volatile, as shown by the rapid fluctuations between regime thresholds over the last three weeks (1).

Scenario Balance:

  • Base Case dominant: "Risk-On" persistence supported by rising net positioning breadth (1).
  • Upside risk: Transition to "Strong Risk-On" if the z-score exceeds the 1.0 threshold (1).
  • Downside risk: Reversion to "Neutral" if crowded long share declines below current levels (1).

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Tactical (weeks): The methodology identifies this as a sentiment filter for tactical allocation (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: High; broad speculative positioning breadth is a primary driver of cross-asset risk appetite.

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs global speculative sentiment and the breadth of market crowding (1).
  • Economic mechanism: Expanding speculative appetite suggests a positive demand impulse for pro-cyclical assets (1).
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Typically requires confirmation from volatility (VIX) or liquidity signals to filter false positives (1).

Regime-Specific Macro Themes

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement (mandatory): Given a 50% speculative crowded long share in Agriculture and a 41.9% hedger deep long share in Energy, this setup aligns with Upward-biased price paths and Normal volatility, where the dominant risk is Trend continuation, not mean reversion (1).
  • The signal currently identifies a dual regime of moderating Inflation Impulse in Agriculture and intensifying Supply Stress in Energy (1).
  • Conviction Band: High; Interpretation Confidence: High Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Improving; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • Inflation_Impulse: Defined by high speculative longs and producer hedging (deep shorts) in Energy or Metals (1).
  • Supply_Stress: Defined by commercial hedgers holding deep long positions in Energy or Agriculture (1).
  • Global_Slowdown: Triggered by Metals shorts combined with a broad risk-off tone (1).
  • Regime-Specific Macro Themes (Latest: 2026-05-12) (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • Agriculture maintains an impulse profile with 50% spec long/hedger short shares, though the intensity has softened from peak levels (1).
  • Metals momentum is rising, evidenced by the average speculative z-score increasing from 0.47 to 0.76 over the last three reports (1).
  • Energy hedgers are increasingly deep long (41.9%), signaling physical market tightness or geopolitical hedging (1).
  • Conditional Invalidation: A sharp decline in Metals speculative z-scores below 0.0 or a collapse in Energy hedger long interest.

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Persistent supply-side constraints in Energy support a bullish bias.
  • Upside risk: A secondary Metals-led inflation impulse if spec z-scores breach extreme thresholds.
  • Downside risk: Transition to Global Slowdown if Metals spec positioning rotates to net-short.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs the pricing and supply stress macro dimensions (1).
  • Economic mechanism: Implies physical market tightness and speculative anticipation of rising input costs.
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Typical interaction: High spec longs in Ags/Metals often precede broader CPI acceleration.

Regime Context:

  • The Supply Stress regime in Energy is persistent and strengthening, with deep long shares rising for three consecutive periods (1).
  • Agriculture's inflation impulse is stabilising after a period of extreme speculative crowding (1).

Model Limitations:

  • Static thresholds for "deep" positioning may require recalibration in high-volatility environments (1).
  • Sector mapping relies on heuristics that may lag sudden structural shifts in market behavior (1).

USD Index Signal

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given a monthly value of 119.28, which sits below the 12-month moving average of 119.86 and reflects a -1.46% six-month change, this setup aligns with Downward-biased price paths and Indeterminate volatility, where the dominant risk is Mean reversion, not Trend continuation (1).
  • The signal is currently classified as Bearish, representing a weakening regime for the U.S. Dollar index (1).
  • Conviction Band: Medium; Interpretation Confidence: High Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Volatile; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • A Weakening regime is defined when the index is below its 12-month moving average or the six-month percentage change is below -5% (1).
  • Price position relative to the 12-month MA determines the core trend state, with a 0.5% hysteresis band often applied to level breaks (1).
  • USD Index Signal (May 01, 2026) (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the price (119.28) falling below the 12-month MA (119.86), triggering the Bearish classification (1).
  • Momentum has shifted lower, with the 6-month change moving from +0.75% in March to -1.46% in May (1).
  • The signal is currently testing the 12-month MA, suggesting a state of inflection rather than deep trend maturity.
  • Conditional Invalidation: A monthly close above 120.46 (approx. MA + 0.5% band) or 6-month momentum exceeding +5% (1).
  • The regime has shown recent volatility, flipping from Bearish to Bullish in March 2026 before returning to Bearish in April (1).

Scenario Balance:

  • Dominant base case: Persistence of a weakening dollar regime as price remains below historical averages.
  • Upside risk: A sharp reversal in global risk appetite driving defensive dollar positioning above the MA.
  • Downside risk: Acceleration of negative momentum toward the -5% threshold, further easing financial conditions.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months) due to the use of 6-month and 12-month lookback windows (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Medium, as the signal is currently near a major regime threshold.

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs global liquidity and financial conditions; a weakening USD acts as a proxy for easing (1).
  • The implied mechanism suggests tailwinds for commodities and non-USD assets due to reduced global funding stress (1).
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Typically interacts negatively with interest rate differentials and positively with risk-on sentiment.

Regime Context:

  • The current regime is a re-entry into a weakening phase following a one-month Bullish interruption (1).
  • Direction of change: Stabilising at lower levels after recent downward momentum.

Model Limitations:

  • Lagging nature due to the use of a 12-month moving average window (1).
  • Static thresholds may fail to adapt to shifts in underlying currency volatility regimes (1).

Data & References:

  • USD Index Signal Dataset (latest observation: May 01, 2026) (1).
  • Influential datapoints: Current Value (119.28) and 12-Month MA (119.86) (1).
  • Additional public datasets: Federal Reserve Broad Dollar Index (H.10), U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yields.
